questions.q: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: **TELEOLOGICAL**
questions.solution:
Teleological describes something explained by its purpose or intended end. Purpose-driven is the matching meaning.

**Answer: Purpose-driven**

Acknowledgement is the correctly spelled noun formed from acknowledge. The other options omit or misplace letters.

**Answer: Acknowledgement**

questions.q: Which of the following sentences uses the word "desert" with the **same meaning** as in the following sentence? "We had to desert the ship after the engine failed"
options: The Mojave Desert is known for its extreme heat.
Many animals that live in the desert are nocturnal.
We found an oasis in the middle of the vast desert.
He would never desert his friends in their time of need.
questions.solution:
To desert a ship means to abandon it. Deserting friends uses the same verb meaning.

**Answer: He would never desert his friends in their time of need.**

Conspicuous means easily noticed. Its spelling is c-o-n-s-p-i-c-u-o-u-s.

**Answer: Conspicuous**

questions.q: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: **See eye to eye**
options: To understand a complex visual concept
To agree fully with someone else
questions.solution:
Seeing eye to eye means sharing the same opinion or agreeing fully.

**Answer: To agree fully with someone else**

questions.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: **Ponderous**
questions.solution:
Ponderous means heavy or cumbersome. Light is its opposite.

**Answer: Light**

questions.q:
**Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A person who is in charge of a ship**
questions.solution:
The captain commands a ship. A sailor is a crew member and need not be in charge.

**Answer: Captain**

questions.q:
**Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A person who studies casually without seriousness.**
questions.solution:
A dilettante takes a casual, superficial interest in a subject, unlike a serious scholar or expert.

**Answer: Dilettante**

questions.q:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The national anthem is sung at the beginning of every match.
options: The national anthem sings at the beginning of every match.
People sing the national anthem at the beginning of every match.
They are singing the national anthem at the beginning of every match.
The national anthem has been sung at the beginning of every match.
questions.solution:
The passive simple present form is sung becomes the active simple present verb sing. People supplies the subject.

**Answer: People sing the national anthem at the beginning of every match.**

questions.q:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

He said, "I finished my project, and I was working on a new one."
options: He said that he had finished his project and he was working on a new one.
He said that he had finished his project and he had been working on a new one.
He said that he finished his project and he had been working on a new one.
He said that he had been finishing his project and he had been working on a new one.
questions.solution:
Reported past simple finished changes to had finished. Past continuous was working changes to had been working.

**Answer: He said that he had finished his project and he had been working on a new one.**

questions.q: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: __**A part of the rural population are migrated**__ to the cities.
options: A parts of the rural population has migrated
A part of the rural populations have migrated
A part of the rural population were migrated
A part of the rural population has migrated
questions.solution:
The subject A part is singular, so it takes has. Migration here is active: has migrated.

**Answer: A part of the rural population has migrated**

questions.q:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

John , a football player who captained his team in school as well as college, __**will be inaugurate**__ the match tomorrow in Pune.
questions.solution:
Use the base verb after will. Therefore, will inaugurate is correct.

**Answer: will inaugurate**

questions.q:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

The archaeologists, after many years of searching, have discovered a hidden ancient tomb.
options: A hidden ancient tomb was discovered by the archaeologists after many years of searching.
A hidden ancient tomb has been discovered by the archaeologists after many years of searching.
A hidden ancient tomb had been discovered by the archaeologists after many years of searching.
A hidden ancient tomb is discovered by the archaeologists after many years of searching.
questions.solution:
Present perfect active have discovered becomes has been discovered with the singular subject a hidden ancient tomb.

**Answer: A hidden ancient tomb has been discovered by the archaeologists after many years of searching.**

questions.q: **Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence**: Why do they always make such a big fuss about trivial matters?
options: Why is such a big fuss always made about trivial matters?
Why such a big fuss is always made about trivial matters?
Why was such a big fuss always made about trivial matters?
Why has such a big fuss always been made about trivial matters?
questions.solution:
A present simple passive question uses is + subject + past participle: Why is such a big fuss always made?

**Answer: Why is such a big fuss always made about trivial matters?**

questions.q: **Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice**. The young boy asked his mother how he could fix his broken toy.
options: The young boy asked, "How could I fix my broken toy?"
The young boy said, "How can he fix his broken toy?"
The young boy said to his mother, "How could he fix his broken toy?"
The young boy asked his mother, "How can I fix my broken toy?"
questions.solution:
The original speaker refers to himself as I. Reported could returns to can in the direct question.

**Answer: The young boy asked his mother, "How can I fix my broken toy?"**

questions.q:
**Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph**:

P. After laying out a grid across the site, the team started to dig out the topsoil layers gently.

Q. They meticulously documented the location of artefacts as they were gradually unearthed using trowels and brushes.

R. Every item they discovered, including old tools and shattered ceramics, was cleaned and catalogued.

S. The artefacts brought the past of a long-lost culture to life by telling a story.
questions.solution:
First the team lays out the grid and digs (P). Then it documents finds (Q), cleans them (R), and explains their significance (S).

**Answer: P, Q, R, S**
